title: Integrability of the weighted Gaussian density derivative
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set, let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\le 1$ for every $z$, let $v>0$, and let $c\in\mathbb R^I$. Then the function sending $z$ to $f(z)$ times the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$ is integrable, as a function valued in the continuous linear functionals on $\mathbb R^I$, with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^I$. Here $p_v(m,t)$ is the density of the Gaussian with mean $m$ and variance $v$.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Write $p_v(c,z)$ for the $N(c,v)$ density when $v>0$ and set $p_0(c,z)=0$; define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and interpret division by zero as zero. Let $A_v(c,z)$ be the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_i\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$. Let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f|\le1$. If $v>0$ and $c\in\mathbb R^I$, then $z\mapsto f(z)A_v(c,z)$ is Lebesgue-integrable as a linear-functional-valued function.
